message.content:
**Killing VS Code (code.exe) from the command line**

On Windows you can terminate the VS Code executable (`code.exe`) with the built‑in `taskkill` utility.  
Below are the most common ways to do it, plus a quick note on why you might need admin rights.

---

### 1️⃣ Basic one‑liner

```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F
```

* `/IM` – *Image name*: specifies the process name (`code.exe`).  
* `/F` – *Force*: forces termination even if the process is hung.

This will close the main VS Code window and all its child processes (the renderer, extensions, etc.) because `code.exe` spawns them.

---

### 2️⃣ Terminate the whole tree (recommended)

If you want to make sure **every** child process spawned by VS Code is also killed, add `/T`:

```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T
```

* `/T` – *Tree*: terminates the specified process and any child processes started by it.

---

### 3️⃣ Use a PID instead of image name

If you already have the Process ID (PID) of the VS Code instance you want to kill, you can target it directly:

```cmd
taskkill /PID <pid> /F
```

Replace `<pid>` with the actual number (e.g., `taskkill /PID 12345 /F`).

---

### 4️⃣ From PowerShell (alternative)

If you prefer PowerShell, the equivalent command is:

```powershell
Stop-Process -Name code -Force
```

or with a specific PID:

```powershell
Stop-Process -Id <pid> -Force
```

---

### ⚠️ Permissions

* If you’re running into “Access denied” errors, try launching the Command Prompt or PowerShell **as Administrator** (right‑click → Run as administrator).  
* In some corporate environments, group policy may restrict terminating certain processes; in that case you’ll need to contact your IT department.

---

### 📌 Quick cheat‑sheet

| Scenario | Command |
|----------|---------|
| Kill all VS Code windows | `taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T` |
| Kill a specific instance by PID | `taskkill /PID 12345 /F` |
| PowerShell alternative | `Stop-Process -Name code -Force` |

That’s it! Once you run the appropriate command, VS Code should exit immediately.
